q: What is CUE and how is it different from reporting data centre Scope 2?
title: Data centre CUE vs Scope 2
short: CUE, carbon usage effectiveness, is the CO2 from all energy a data centre uses divided by its IT equipment energy, in kg CO2 per IT kWh. Scope 2 is an absolute total of purchased electricity emissions only. CUE is a ratio, includes diesel generators, and is for tracking efficiency, not for your inventory.
audience: Data centre operators and colocation customers

p: CUE = total CO2 from data centre energy / IT equipment energy in kWh. Total CO2 covers grid electricity and on-site generation such as diesel sets. For a site that runs only on grid power, CUE equals PUE x the grid factor, so with grid power alone it moves with both cooling efficiency and the grid's carbon intensity.

sections.h: Four ways it differs from Scope 2
ul: Units: CUE is kg CO2 per IT kWh; Scope 2 is tonnes CO2 for the year.
Sources: CUE adds diesel generator fuel, which your inventory puts in Scope 1, not Scope 2.
Boundary: CUE covers only the data centre space. Scope 2 covers every site in your organisational boundary.
Purpose: CUE compares a site against itself over time. Scope 2 goes into a GHG inventory and BRSR or buyer reports.

p: CUE can be computed with either grid factor. State which. In India the location-based figure uses the CEA weighted average; a market-based figure needs certificates or a green tariff with matching units. Do not mix them across years or sites.

Your provider's CUE describes their whole site. Your own emissions come from your metered IT kWh x their PUE x the grid factor, and whether that sits in your Scope 2 or Scope 3 depends on who buys the electricity. Ask for the provider's CUE basis and period before quoting it.

example.title: Illustrative example: one year with a diesel backup set
lines: Grid electricity: 510,000 kWh x 0.710 = 362,100 kg CO2 (Scope 2)
DG diesel: 4,000 litres x 2.68 = 10,720 kg CO2 (Scope 1)
IT energy at UPS output: 300,000 kWh
Grid only check: PUE 1.70 x 0.710 = 1.21, matching 362,100 / 300,000
example.note: Figures are illustrative. Factors: CEA CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0 and the IPCC 2006 diesel default.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (billing period, tariff category, sanctioned load, units) and applies the CEA grid factor of 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0, for location-based Scope 2, and reads diesel invoices at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre for Scope 1.
